result.title: Neural Compression for Scientific Particle Data: Perspectives on How Learning Can Help
result.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Extended version of paper accepted at 2026 Conference on Physics and AI (PAI26)
result.summary: As particle-based simulations grow in scale, efficient compression of scientific data becomes critical. Neural point cloud compression (PCC) methods excel on computer vision (CV) benchmarks, but do they transfer to scientific particle data? We highlight that scientific particles differ from CV point clouds in fractal dimension: CV point clouds are locally planar, but particles are not. This key difference limits the effectiveness of the octree data structure that underpins most PCC methods. Neural codecs achieve only marginal bitrate reductions over the traditional G-PCC baseline on scientific data, revealing a significant performance gap. Supported by an evaluation spanning domains of cosmology, molecular dynamics, and plasma physics, we outline where the structure of scientific data limits current neural approaches and where learning can help in the future.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文考察神经点云压缩能否迁移到科学粒子数据，指出科学粒子与 CV 点云在分形维数上的差异削弱了八叉树结构的适用性，并通过宇宙学、分子动力学与等离子体物理三域评估显示神经编解码相对传统 G-PCC 仅带来有限比特率收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察是数据几何（局部平面性 vs. 分形维数）决定编码结构与压缩效率，可能为 LVR 中视觉细节在 latent 中的保真度、表示坍缩与信息瓶颈评价提供类比视角，但该文不涉及多模态推理，迁移线索需核查。
